title: Profiting from the Decoy Effect: A Case Study of an Online Diamond Retailer
eligible_reason: Structural choice model of diamond sales with decoy/dominance relations among same-grade diamonds, estimated by ML (Tomlab/KNITRO, GPU) on a daily SKU panel from an online diamond retailer; pricing counterfactuals. No binary staggered treatment and no DiD or event study.
design_notes: main.m -> data.m (index, diamond_X, season_Z, market_W, dominance_D, sales_y) and ll_fn.m log-likelihood; output_mle.txt. Regression inventory empty (MATLAB only).
data_files_note: README: 'a sample panel of 50,000 diamonds (74,638 diamonds were used in the paper)'; sampling rule not stated.
data_provenance_note: 67% sample of the estimation diamonds; sampling rule not stated (closest category, as mksc.2019.1165). Moot because the design is not a DiD.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally (data/text/mksc and papers/mksc checked Nov 2); OpenAlex abstract read from data/frame/mksc.jsonl. Design read from the README and the main-results code; no package code was run.
